title: Unilever — AI predictive maintenance for consumer goods manufacturing
content:
Unilever deployed an AI-driven predictive maintenance system at its Indaiatuba plant in Brazil, one of its largest Latin American facilities manufacturing home and personal care products. The factory faced high maintenance costs and frequent unplanned downtime caused by critical asset issues like compressor bearing wear, HVAC condenser fouling, and packaging line servo motor degradation. Traditional time-based preventive maintenance was inefficient, leading to missed degradation patterns and unexpected failures.

To solve this, the plant partnered with iFactory to implement an on-premise AI predictive maintenance platform. They installed over 50,000 IoT sensors across compressors, HVAC units, and packaging machinery to capture real-time operational signals. These sensor streams were fed into a unified data lake, where machine learning models trained on five years of historical failure data generated remaining-useful-life predictions. The system was integrated with Unilever’s CMMS to auto-generate and prioritize work orders for technicians before failures occurred.

The deployment yielded significant financial and operational improvements. Unilever achieved a 45% reduction in annual maintenance spend, saving $2.3 million against a $5.1 million baseline. Unplanned downtime was slashed by 40%, dropping from 8.2% to 4.9%. Additionally, the plant sustained an Overall Equipment Effectiveness of over 85% for two consecutive years, recovering its $1.2 million investment in under seven months.

title: FIH Mobile — Google Cloud Visual Inspection AI for PCB assembly
content:
FIH Mobile, a subsidiary of Foxconn Technology Group, faced quality control challenges in its smartphone manufacturing operations. During the pre-production phase of printed circuit board (PCB) assembly, the company relied on manual human inspection to identify defects like missing screws or solder bridging. This manual process was slow, inconsistent across stations, and suffered from a critical defect escape rate of 40%—meaning two-fifths of defective units initially went unnoticed.

To solve this, FIH Mobile built an automated quality assurance system using Google Cloud's AutoML Vision. Deploying this deep learning-based computer vision platform directly onto its inspection stations allowed the manufacturer to run real-time, standardized evaluations on every PCB.

The deployment delivered a dramatic improvement in both speed and accuracy. FIH Mobile successfully reduced its PCB defect escape rate from 40% to 10%. Furthermore, the automated system reduced the inspection time for each component to just 0.3 seconds—or 1.3 seconds when factoring in physical fixture movement—while standardizing quality gates across all its assembly lines.

title: General Motors — iFactory AI production planning platform
content: General Motors, a major automotive manufacturer operating 31 plants across North America, faced severe production planning inefficiencies in its complex supply chain. The company's legacy systems suffered from demand forecast errors of 22% to 28%, which forced excessive safety stock buffers, inflated inventory carrying costs, and resulted in $2.8 billion in annual waste across its operations. To solve these critical challenges, General Motors deployed the iFactory AI Production Planning platform. This advanced system built machine learning forecasting models that analyze 24 months of production history, 8,000 supplier data points, and real-time sales signals. The technique allows the system to predict demand 12 to 18 weeks forward with 94% accuracy, optimize real-time line sequencing, and synchronize delivery schedules with 3,000 critical suppliers. Within eight weeks of deploying this AI-powered forecasting and planning solution, the company achieved measurable operational and financial outcomes. Specifically, General Motors reduced direct material waste by 30%, improved on-time delivery from 84% to 96%, decreased its annual inventory carrying costs by $480 million, and freed $1.8 billion in working capital.

title: Cipla — AI-driven job shop scheduling system
content: Cipla India, a major global pharmaceutical manufacturer, faced significant operational bottlenecks at its oral solid dosage plant in Indore. Due to strict current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) regulations, transition times between products on the factory floor were highly inefficient. Each changeover required extensive, time-consuming equipment cleaning and setup procedures to prevent cross-contamination, which strained overall productivity. To resolve this, the company implemented an AI-driven job shop scheduling system. The technique involved deploying machine learning algorithms that integrated with their digital manufacturing systems to analyze and automate scheduling. The AI optimized production sequencing by systematically replacing major cleanup and setup procedures with minor ones. This kept the facility fully compliant with regulatory standards while reducing idle line time. The published outcome of this digital scheduling deployment was a 22 percent reduction in equipment changeover durations. Additionally, the intelligent automation and enhanced supply chain visibility delivered by the system enabled Cipla to cut its overall manufacturing costs at the Indore facility by 26 percent.

title: NSG Group — AI Computer Vision Workplace Safety Platform
content: NSG Group, a global manufacturer of glass and glazing products, faced the challenge of maintaining workplace safety standards and reducing compliance risks across its vast multinational operations. Given the high-risk nature of glass manufacturing, manual monitoring of safety protocols was insufficient to consistently capture hazards. To address this, NSG Group partnered with Voxel to implement an AI-powered computer vision platform integrated with their existing CCTV infrastructure. The system leverages deep learning techniques to continuously analyze live video feeds, automatically identifying leading indicators of safety risks in real-time. This includes tracking personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance, monitoring ergonomic hazards like improper lifting, and identifying unauthorized pedestrian zone violations. Following a global rollout across facilities in ten countries, the company reported substantial, measured improvements. In a United States facility, the deployment led to a 62% reduction in safety vest compliance incidents within the first 30 days. Additionally, a Canadian facility documented a 57% decrease in ergonomic risk events, specifically improper bends, between the third and fourth quarters of 2024, while a Malaysian plant recorded a 75% reduction in person-to-equipment proximity events within three months. This automated approach allowed safety managers to shift from reactive incident reporting to proactive, data-driven coaching and interventions.
